mainTopic: מלקות for a לאו with no action, lashes plus payment for muzzling an animal, רב פפא's two rulings (milk dough and mixed species in a pen), and helping animals mate.
overview: The amud opens at the end of רבי יוחנן's proof from the משנה in תמורה, which gives forty lashes for swapping a קרבן even though the swap is done only by speech. ריש לקיש answers that this משנה follows רבי יהודה, who gives מלקות even for a לאו with no action. The גמרא challenges this because the same משנה includes a יורש, which רבי יהודה rejects. It answers that a תנא can agree with רבי יהודה on one point and disagree on another. Next, a ברייתא rules that someone who muzzles a threshing cow gets מלקות and also pays for its food, which seems to break the rule that one sin brings only one punishment. אביי, רבא and רב פפא each give a different answer. רב פפא then reports two questions he forbade: kneading dough with milk, where he was right, and putting different species in one pen, where he was not, since שמואל holds that כלאים needs a direct act. The amud ends with רב יהודה permitting someone to help same-species animals mate, because he is busy with his work, and a challenge from רב אחדבוי בר אמי that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the proof: swapping a קרבן brings forty lashes
steps.stepSummary: The quote from the משנה in תמורה finishes: swapping is forbidden, but if done it works, and the person gets forty lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: This does not mean a person is allowed to swap an animal for a קרבן. It means that if he did swap, the swap works, and he gets the forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote that רבי יוחנן brought as proof from the משנה in תמורה. That משנה says someone who swaps a regular animal for a קרבן gets forty lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A swap (תמורה) is made only by saying words, with no physical action. Yet the משנה says the swapper gets מלקות. So רבי יוחנן's point is that words alone can count enough to earn מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: to swap a regular animal for one that is already a קרבן
the swap takes effect, so the new animal becomes holy too
literally 'absorbs the forty', meaning he receives מלקות
the forbidden swap of an animal for a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is NOT saying swapping is allowed. It is forbidden. It only says that if someone does it anyway, it still works.

phrases.english: Not that a person is permitted to swap,
rather, that if he swapped, the swap takes effect,
and he receives the forty lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the source רבי יוחנן cited just before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That a לאו done only through speech can earn מלקות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה at the start of מסכת תמורה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: that משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the משנה in תמורה follows רבי יהודה, who gives מלקות even for a לאו with no action.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: whose opinion is this? It is רבי יהודה, who says that we give lashes for a לאו that has no action.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש pushes away רבי יוחנן's proof. He says the משנה matches only רבי יהודה's personal view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that even a לאו with no action at all earns מלקות. So a משנה following him proves nothing for the other חכמים, who need a real action. ריש לקיש's own view can follow those חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'whose is this?', a way of tying a source to one specific תנא
a prohibition broken without any physical action

phrases.english: He said to him: whose opinion is this?
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש is answering רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: It is רבי יהודה,
who says: a prohibition that has no action,
we flog for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the משנה to רבי יהודה's view, so it is not a general proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the משנה follows everyone, but it may follow only רבי יהודה.

steps.title: But the same משנה includes an heir, which רבי יהודה rejects
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can be רבי יהודה's, when its first line includes a יורש and רבי יהודה says a יורש cannot swap.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say this follows רבי יהודה? The first line teaches: 'Everyone can swap, men and women alike.' We asked what 'everyone' adds, and answered: an heir. That is not like רבי יהודה, since he says an heir cannot swap and an heir does not do סמיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's answer. It points to the first line of the same משנה, which already disagrees with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'everyone' was explained elsewhere as including a יורש, someone who inherited his father's קרבן. רבי יהודה holds a יורש cannot make a swap. So the first line seems to go against רבי יהודה, and the whole משנה should not be his.

keyTerms.meaning: 'can you really set it up as...?', opening a challenge
the first part of a משנה
does סמיכה, leaning hands on a קרבן

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: But can you establish it as following רבי יהודה?
But it teaches in the first clause:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מְמִירִין, אֶחָד הָאֲנָשִׁים וְאֶחָד הַנָּשִׁים,
phrases.english: Everyone can swap, both men and women,
and we discussed it: 'everyone' comes to include what?
To include an heir, and that is not like רבי יהודה,
phrases.notes: He means someone who inherited an animal his father had made a קרבן.

phrases.english: for if it were like רבי יהודה, doesn't he say:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ מֵמִיר, יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ סוֹמֵךְ!
phrases.english: an heir cannot swap, an heir does not lean his hands!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's claim that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה in תמורה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first line includes a יורש, and רבי יהודה rejects that, so the משנה looks like it does not follow him.

steps.title: The תנא agrees with רבי יהודה on one point only
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this תנא follows רבי יהודה about lashes without an action, but argues with him about the heir.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא agrees with him on one point and disagrees with him on one point.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and saves ריש לקיש's position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תנא does not have to follow one opinion on every topic. This תנא can agree with רבי יהודה that a לאו with no action earns מלקות, while disagreeing about a יורש. So ריש לקיש's answer still holds, and רבי יוחנן's proof is still pushed away.

keyTerms.meaning: a sage of the משנה period

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's answer stands. The משנה in תמורה follows רבי יהודה about a לאו with no action, so it does not prove רבי יוחנן's view.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּווֹתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא,
phrases.english: This תנא holds like him in one matter,
phrases.notes: The 'one matter' he agrees on is getting lashes for a לאו with no action.

phrases.english: and disagrees with him in one matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּווֹתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting a תנא's views: he agrees with רבי יהודה on one law but not on another.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A משנה that argues with רבי יהודה on one point cannot follow him on any point.
steps.terutzMaskana: A תנא can follow רבי יהודה about a לאו with no action and still include a יורש.

steps.title: Muzzling a working cow: lashes and payment
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one who muzzles a cow while threshing gets מלקות and also pays for the food it would have eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: one who muzzles a cow and threshes with it gets lashes. He also pays four קבים for a cow and three קבים for a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about muzzling an animal during work. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Muzzling a working animal breaks the לאו of לא תחסום. The ברייתא gives two results: מלקות, and paying the owner for the food the animal was kept from eating. The amounts are four קבים for a cow and three for a donkey.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: one who muzzles the cow
and threshes with it is flogged,
and pays four קבים for a cow,
phrases.notes: This is the amount of food the animal would have eaten while working.

phrases.english: and three קבים for a donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַחוֹסֵם אֶת הַפָּרָה וְדָשׁ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא on the same subject of muzzling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who muzzles a threshing animal gets מלקות and also pays for its food.

steps.title: But one sin brings only one punishment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא can give both מלקות and payment, when the rule is that one sin gets only one punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't there a rule that a person does not get lashes and death, and does not get lashes and also pay?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא with a well-known rule against double punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The standard rule is that one act brings only one punishment. You cannot get both מלקות and death, or both מלקות and a payment. The ברייתא gives both, so it seems to break this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: one is not given lashes and also death for one act
one is not given lashes and also made to pay for one act

phrases.english: But isn't it that one is not flogged and put to death,
and one is not flogged and made to pay?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the double punishment in the ברייתא from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling of both מלקות and payment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known rule says one sin gets only one punishment, and the ברייתא gives two.

steps.title: אביי: the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who holds that a person can get מלקות and also pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: whose opinion is this? It is רבי מאיר, who says a person can be flogged and also pay.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by tying the ברייתא to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'one punishment only' rule is not held by everyone. רבי מאיר holds that מלקות and payment can both apply. So the ברייתא follows him and does not contradict itself.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא giving both מלקות and payment for muzzling follows רבי מאיר, who allows both punishments together.

phrases.english: Abaye said: whose opinion is this?
It is רבי מאיר,
who says: one is flogged and pays.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tying the ברייתא to a specific תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone holds that one sin brings only one punishment, so the ברייתא contradicts the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who allows both מלקות and payment.

steps.title: רבא: A person can owe money even when no court makes him pay
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the question from Step 6 by pointing to אתנן. The Torah forbids it even when the man committed a death-penalty sin, where no court would ever make him pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The Torah forbade an אתנן even if the man had relations with his own mother.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the question of how muzzling can bring both מלקות and payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man who sins with his mother deserves death, so a court would never make him pay anything. Still, the Torah treats his payment to her as a real אתנן, so the money obligation must exist anyway. In the same way, the one who muzzles gets מלקות from the court, yet he still truly owes the owner for the food, even though the court will not force him to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal given as payment to a זונה; it may not be brought as a קרבן
Had relations with his mother, a sin that carries the death penalty

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say the court collects both punishments. The court gives lashes. The money is still truly owed, but the court does not force him to pay it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The Torah forbade a harlot's payment,
and even if he had relations with his mother.
phrases.notes: That sin carries the death penalty, so no court would make him pay. Still, his payment counts as an אתנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the קשיא of Step 6, in place of אביי's answer in Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separates the court's punishment from the money a person truly owes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since one sin gets one punishment, a person who gets מלקות cannot owe any money at all
steps.terutzMaskana: He gets מלקות in court, but he still truly owes the money, just as an אתנן counts as payment even when the court cannot make him pay

steps.title: רב פפא: The food debt started before the sin
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the duty to feed the cow began when he pulled it, while the lashes come only when he muzzles it. So these are two separate obligations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: From the moment he pulled the cow, he became obligated to feed it. He does not get lashes until the moment he muzzles it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a third answer to the same question from Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of one punishment per sin only applies when both punishments come from the same act at the same moment. Here the duty to feed the cow began earlier, at משיכה, when he took the cow. The sin, and so the lashes, only comes later at חסימה, so the payment is not a second punishment for the sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling an animal, which makes the deal take effect

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
From the time of pulling
phrases.notes: When he pulled the cow to take it for threshing, the deal took effect.

phrases.english: he became obligated to him for its food,
but lashes he does not receive
until the time of muzzling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another alternative answer to the קשיא of Step 6, alongside אביי and רבא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separates the two obligations by time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lashes and payment both come from the one act of muzzling
steps.terutzMaskana: The food debt began at משיכה and the lashes only at חסימה, so they are two separate obligations
steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers to Step 6. אביי says the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר. רבא says the money is truly owed even without the court. רב פפא says the two obligations start at different times.

steps.title: רב פפא introduces two questions he was asked
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the household of רב פפא בר אבא asked him two questions. He forbade both, but only one of his rulings matched the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The household of רב פפא בר אבא asked me these matters. I ruled both forbidden. One ruling was according to the הלכה, and one was not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new topic. רב פפא tells us he will share two questions and his rulings on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is an introduction. It tells us ahead of time that both rulings were 'forbidden.' It also tells us one ruling was correct and one was not. The details come in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
These matters were asked of me
by the household of Rav Pappa bar Abba,
and I resolved them for them as forbidden:
one in accordance with the halacha,
and one not in accordance with the halacha.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּעוֹ מִינַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב פפא, who just spoke in Step 9, now opens a new topic of his own
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Of רב פפא's two 'forbidden' rulings, one matched the הלכה and one did not

steps.title: The first question: kneading dough with milk
steps.stepSummary: The first question was whether one may knead dough with milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked me: What is the law about kneading dough with milk?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא tells us the first of the two questions he was asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dough kneaded with milk makes dairy bread, which looks like regular bread. The question is whether making such bread is allowed.

phrases.english: They asked me:
What is the law about kneading dough with milk?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינַּאי: מַהוּ לָלוּשׁ אֶת הָעִיסָּה בְּחָלָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first of the two questions announced in Step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may knead dough with milk

steps.title: Forbidden, and a ברייתא agrees
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא forbade it, and this ruling matches the הלכה. A ברייתא says bread kneaded with milk is forbidden. It says the same about bread baked in an oven smeared with tail fat, until the oven is heated.
steps.simpleTranslation: I ruled it forbidden, in line with the הלכה, as a ברייתא teaches: One may not knead dough with milk. If he did, the whole loaf is forbidden, because people may come to sin by habit. In the same way, one may not smear an oven with tail fat. If he did, all the bread is forbidden until he heats the oven.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives his answer, forbidden, and brings a ברייתא to show that this ruling is the correct הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Milky bread looks like plain bread, so a person may eat it with meat by habit. That is why the whole loaf is forbidden. The oven case works the same way. Bread baked in an oven smeared with fat may be eaten with dairy, so it is forbidden until the oven is heated empty.

keyTerms.meaning: Becoming used to sin; a habit that leads to sin
The fat of an animal's tail

steps.whatToRemember: Bread made with milk, or baked in an oven smeared with fat, is forbidden. People might eat it with the opposite kind of food without noticing.

phrases.english: And I resolved it for them as forbidden,
in accordance with the halacha, as it is taught in a baraita:
One may not knead dough with milk,
and if he kneaded it,
the entire loaf is forbidden,
because of becoming accustomed to sin.
Similarly:
One may not smear the oven with tail fat,
and if he smeared it,
all of the bread is forbidden,
until he heats the oven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of Step 11 and backs the answer with a ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Kneading dough with milk is forbidden, and the whole loaf becomes forbidden
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's ruling that kneading dough with milk is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding milky dough and bread baked in an oven smeared with tail fat, because of הרגל עבירה

steps.title: The second question: different species in one pen
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's second question was whether you may bring a male and a female of different species into one pen.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other question they asked me was: may you bring one species together with a different species into a pen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second of the two questions from Step 10. It sets up רב פפא's answer, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the animals might mate on their own, and that would be כלאים, mixing species. The question is whether just setting up that situation is already forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: One species and a different species

phrases.english: And the other question they asked of me:
phrases.notes: This is the second of the two questions from the household of רב פפא בר אבא.

phrases.english: What is the law about bringing in
one species and another that is not its species into the pen?
phrases.notes: He means a male and a female of different kinds, which might mate with each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first question (Steps 11-12) to the second question announced in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is it forbidden to put different species together in one pen, where they might mate?

steps.title: רב פפא forbade it, but that was not the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא forbade it, and he admits this ruling does not match the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I answered them that it is forbidden, but that was not in line with the הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives his answer to the second question and admits it was the ruling that went wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said only one of his two rulings matched the הלכה. The milk-dough ruling was correct, so this one, about the pen, is the mistake. The real הלכה is that putting the animals together is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in line with the הלכה

phrases.english: And I resolved it for them as forbidden,
which is not in accordance with the הלכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13 and identifies it as the incorrect ruling from Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב פפא forbade it, but the actual הלכה permits it.

steps.title: שמואל: liability for כלאים needs a direct act
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that for כלאים, a person is liable only when he himself inserts the animal's organ, like a brush into a tube.
steps.simpleTranslation: As שמואל says: for adulterers, it is enough that the witnesses see them acting the way adulterers act. But for כלאים, he is liable only when he inserts like a brush into a tube.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל to prove why forbidding the pen was not the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says the sin of כלאים is the person's own act of bringing the animals together, 'like a brush into a tube.' Animals that mate by themselves in a pen are not the person's act. So just putting them together is not forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixing species, here mating two kinds of animals
Like a brush into a tube, a direct act of inserting

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the איסור of mating animals of different kinds is about what the person does with his own hands, not about allowing it to happen.

phrases.english: As שמואל says:
And with adulterers,
phrases.notes: שמואל is talking about what the witnesses must see before there is a punishment.

phrases.english: once they are seen in the manner of adulterers.
But with כלאים,
only once he inserts like a brush into a tube.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason the ruling in Step 14 was not the הלכה.
steps.raayaObject: That putting different species together in a pen is allowed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל: liability for כלאים needs a direct act of inserting, like a brush into a tube.

steps.title: Challenge: does a ברייתא forbid even holding the animal?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי בר אמי quotes a ברייתא that seems to forbid even holding the female animal when the animals are of different kinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחדבוי בר אמי objects: if the Torah had only said 'Do not let your animals mate,' I would have said a person may not even hold the animal while a male mounts it. So the פסוק says 'of different kinds.' Doesn't that imply that with different kinds, even holding is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחדבוי בר אמי challenges שמואל with a ברייתא about holding the animal during mating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the word 'כלאים' limits the איסור to different kinds, so holding is allowed for the same kind. That seems to imply that with different kinds, even holding is forbidden. If just helping is forbidden, then putting them in a pen might be forbidden too, against שמואל.

phrases.english: רב אחדבוי בר אמי raises an objection:
Had it said only
'Do not let your animals mate,'
I would have said
a person may not hold the animal
while a male mounts it.
So the פסוק says 'of different kinds.'
Doesn't it imply
that with different kinds, even holding is not allowed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's rule from Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that only a direct act of inserting counts as כלאים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies that just holding the animal is forbidden with different kinds, so the איסור seems to cover more than inserting.

steps.title: 'Holding' is a polite word for inserting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'holding' in the ברייתא really means inserting, and it is just a polite way to say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'holding' mean? Inserting. And why does it call it 'holding'? To use clean language.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining a word in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used 'holding' as a polite word for the direct act of inserting. So it does not forbid just helping, and it agrees with שמואל. Putting animals together in a pen stays allowed, as stated in Step 14.
steps.whatToRemember: Only a direct act of inserting counts as the sin of כלאים with animals. So letting two kinds share a pen is allowed, and רב פפא's ruling forbidding it was not the הלכה.
steps.confusionAlert: The word 'holding' in this ברייתא does not mean grabbing the animal. It is a polite word for the act of inserting itself.

phrases.english: What does 'holding' mean?
Inserting.
And why does it call it 'holding'?
To use clean language.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 16 and keeps שמואל's rule in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Holding' means just grabbing the animal, so any help is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Holding' is a polite word for inserting, so only the direct act is forbidden, just as שמואל said.

steps.title: רב יהודה permits helping same-species animals mate
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that with animals of the same species, a person may insert the male's organ into the female like a brush into a tube, and there is not even a concern of immodesty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: when the animals are the same species, a person is allowed to insert the male's organ, like putting a brush into a tube. There is not even a problem of immodesty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a new ruling. If both animals are the same species, a person may help them mate by hand, and it is not even considered immodest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 15-17 were about different species, where inserting by hand counts as forbidden כלאים. Here רב יהודה says that with the same species there is no כלאים problem at all. He goes further and says there is not even a lesser problem of improper thoughts (פריצותא).

keyTerms.meaning: A species with its own species: both animals are the same kind
Immodesty; a concern about improper thoughts

steps.whyThisMatters: It draws a clear line: the act that is forbidden with different species is fully permitted with the same species, even regarding modesty.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
A species with its own species,
it is permitted to insert, like a brush into a tube,
phrases.notes: This is the same picture שמואל used in step 15.

phrases.english: and there is not even a concern of immodesty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the different-species case (steps 15-17) to the same-species case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With animals of the same species, a person may insert the organ by hand, and there is no concern of immodesty.

steps.title: Why is there no concern of immodesty?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב יהודה's ruling that there is no immodesty concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב יהודה is not worried about immodest thoughts. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might expect that handling animals during mating could lead a person to improper thoughts. The question asks what makes רב יהודה confident that this is not a problem.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is there no concern of immodesty when a person helps same-species animals mate?

steps.title: He is busy with his work
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the person is occupied with his work, so his mind will not wander to improper thoughts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is busy with his work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The person is focused on his job of breeding animals, so improper thoughts are not a worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is about the person's state of mind, not the act itself. Someone doing this as part of his work is focused on the task, so the act does not lead to פריצותא.
steps.whatToRemember: Same species: inserting by hand is permitted with no immodesty concern, because the person is busy with his work.

phrases.english: He is occupied with his work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person busy with his work does not come to improper thoughts.

steps.title: רב אחדבוי בר אמי begins a challenge
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי בר אמי raises an objection to רב יהודה's ruling. The content of the objection comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחדבוי בר אמי raised an objection:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא tells us a challenge is coming against רב יהודה, and the actual source is quoted in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מתיב means he is bringing a source that seems to contradict the ruling just given. Here the target is רב יהודה's statement that there is no immodesty concern. This is the same רב אחדבוי בר אמי who challenged in step 16.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥadvoi bar Ami raises an objection:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to the ruling given in steps 18-20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling that inserting by hand for same-species animals is permitted with no immodesty concern.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source will be brought that seems to contradict this ruling. Its content appears in the next part of the text.
